question.text: Under the PFRDA (Retirement Adviser) Regulations, 2016, who is required to obtain a certificate of registration?

answer.text: Any individual or non-individual providing retirement advice on NPS or other PFRDA-regulated pension schemes
Only insurance companies selling annuity products
Only chartered accountants providing financial advice

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII pages 231 and 237-238, any individual or non-individual (firm, body corporate, trust, society) desirous of providing retirement advice on NPS or other PFRDA-regulated pension schemes must obtain a certificate of registration. The Trap: Banks may register as Points of Presence (PoPs) and may also act as retirement advisers if registered; page 237 explicitly refers to retirement advisers that are banks, NBFCs and body corporates providing distribution or execution services. Registration is therefore not limited to banks offering NPS services. Note: Certain professionals (advocates, CAs, CSs, cost accountants, actuaries) are exempt when retirement advice is incidental to their practice but must still comply with general obligations.
